title: From idea to architecture
summary: One human-agent collaboration cycle, grounded in Topocode's documented workflow—not a trace of one CLI process. The CLI supplies deterministic evidence and objective checks; the agent interprets and authors; you judge whether the explanation is meaningful. Feedback loops back to interpretation/authoring, and source changes may require another scan. Scan is useful here but not a prerequisite for authored stories.

sections.title: You
sections.body: Set the question and scope. Review meaning, accuracy, and usefulness. Feedback starts another iteration; your approval, not a green check, accepts the architecture document.

sections.title: Coding agent
sections.body: Read code and scan evidence, enrich the understanding, and author an anchored story. Repair diagnostics, preserve story identity, and commit only with authorization. Present the result for human review. Interpretation here does not require the separate topo enrich command.

sections.title: Topocode CLI
sections.body: Initialize and optionally scan the repository without calling a model. Validate drafts and render committed stories. serve supplies a local viewer; bundle supplies static files. These are separate invocations across the collaboration cycle, not one long-running call.

sections.title: Repository
sections.body: Holds source code, configuration, and authored stories. The agent writes and commits the story; the CLI reads source and generates disposable cache/output. This is a file and Git boundary, not a separate hosted service.
